name: Liechtenstein
system_note: The prince holds unusually strong powers, including a veto over laws.
snapshot: An Alpine principality where the prince retains real power, the economy runs on finance and industry, and the head of government has been a woman since 2025.
culture: Liechtenstein's princely family, among Europe's richest, owns one of the world's great private art collections. German is the official language. Vaduz, the capital, is small enough to walk across. Liechtenstein uses the Swiss franc and shares an open border with Switzerland.
society: Liechtenstein has one of the highest incomes per head in the world, with more jobs than residents; many workers commute from Switzerland and Austria. Once a notorious tax haven, it has adopted international transparency rules. Industrial firms like Hilti are major employers. Women only won the vote in 1984.
situation: Brigitte Haas of the Patriotic Union became head of government in 2025, the first woman in the post. Prince Hans-Adam II remains head of state, with day-to-day duties delegated to his son, Hereditary Prince Alois.
power: A constitutional monarchy with strong direct democracy. The prince appoints the government on parliament's proposal and can veto laws, and citizens can force referendums.

leaders.state: Prince Hans-Adam II, with Hereditary Prince Alois as regent
